conventions.commitment: Every quantity below is defined here, in SI-free cosmological units (Mpc, km/s/Mpc, densities as fractions of the critical density), and is the only meaning the gate, the prototype and any later lesson may give it.

recombinationRedshift.definition: z_star is the redshift of recombination (the peak of the photon visibility function in the Boltzmann code that defines it). It is an INPUT of every function of the gate: no fitting formula for it is implemented, because its coefficients are published data (request F1).
recombinationRedshift.designDomain: z_star in [800, 1500]; outside it the function refuses with code bad-recombination-redshift. This is a DESIGN domain of the integral, not the domain of any cited fitting formula; that domain is part of request F1 and is NOT COMMITTED here.

soundHorizon.definition: r_s(z_star) = Int_0^{a_star} c_s c da / (a^2 H(a)), a_star = 1/(1 + z_star), c_s = 1/sqrt(3 (1 + R)), R = 3 rho_b / (4 rho_gamma) = (3 omegaB / (4 omegaGamma)) a, a^2 H = H0 sqrt(Om a + Or + Ok a^2 + Ode a^(1 - 3 w)) finite at a = 0, in Mpc, comoving.
soundHorizon.whyTheIntegral: r_s must come from the integral: DECISIONS_2026-11-07.md and BAO_GATE.md section 10 record that the Eisenstein and Hu 1998 fitting formula for the sound horizon fails its legs and that the drag-redshift fit is 3.7 percent from the printed value; no fitting formula stands in for the integral anywhere in this gate.
soundHorizon.radiation: omegaGamma from T = 2.7255 K (astropy 6.0.1's Planck18 Tcmb0, read by the oracle from the installed data file and pinned) with the exact SI constants and G from astropy.constants; photons plus massless neutrinos with Neff = 3.046 give Or h^2 = omegaGamma (1 + (7/8)(4/11)^(4/3) Neff). Generic worlds (groups relation, oracle, refusals) use this massless treatment; the published comparison (P1, P2) models one 0.06 eV species by its Fermi-Dirac density as P1c of the 257 follow-up did.
soundHorizon.massiveNeutrino: For P1 and P2 only: one of the three species of weight Neff/3 has mass m = 0.06 eV with density rho_nu(a) = rho_gamma(a) (7/8)(4/11)^(4/3) (Neff/3) f(y0 a), f(y) = [Int_0^inf x^2 sqrt(x^2 + y^2) / (e^x + 1) dx] / (7 pi^4/120), y0 = m / (k T_nu0), T_nu0 = (4/11)^(1/3) T; the other two are massless; the cosmological constant is chosen to close flatness today. D_M(z_star) uses the same E(a).

angularDiameterDistance.definition: D_M(z_star) is the comoving transverse (angular-diameter-comoving) distance at z_star, in Mpc: D_M = (c/H0) S_k(chi), chi = Int_0^{z_star} dz / E(z), S_k = sinh(sqrt(Ok) chi)/sqrt(Ok) (Ok > 0), chi (Ok = 0), sin(sqrt(-Ok) chi)/sqrt(-Ok) (Ok < 0), with radiation included in E, supplied by the 255 kernel (js/kernels/cosmology/late, validated to z = 1100 against astropy). The angular-diameter distance is D_M/(1 + z_star), and the gate always uses the comoving D_M with the comoving r_s.

acousticScale.theta: theta_star = r_s(z_star) / D_M(z_star), in radians, the angle subtended by the comoving sound horizon; 100 theta_star is the number a CMB paper prints (about 1.04 for the Planck cosmology); theta_MC (the code's approximation) is not used.
acousticScale.ellA: ell_A = pi / theta_star, the acoustic multipole (the spacing of the peaks).
acousticScale.firstPeak: the position of the m-th peak is ell_m = ell_A (m - phi_m); for m = 1, ell_1 = ell_A (1 - phi_1). The offset phi_1 is a phase shift (driving, the early-ISW effect, the baryon-photon ratio) that depends weakly on the parameters; its cited fitting formula is published data and is request F2. In this gate phi_1 is an INPUT with design domain [0, 0.5]; outside it the function refuses with code bad-offset. A value of phi_1 used in a leg is labelled DESIGN, never the cited offset.
acousticScale.inverse: theta_star = pi (1 - phi_1) / ell_1: the geometry a lesson may read from the first peak's position is theta_star under the stated offset, then D_M(z_star) = r_s / theta_star at an r_s the lesson states with its inputs; an Omega_k or a curvature statement is conditional on those inputs and on the offset, and is never unconditional.

claimRule.rule: A lesson reads the geometry (the angular scale, theta_star, D_M(z_star), and a curvature statement conditional on stated inputs) from the position of the first peak through the stated relation. It NEVER reads a Hubble constant, a matter or baryon density or any composition from which precomputed grid spectrum looks closest to a measured spectrum; a grid is a comparison drawn at the grid node nearest to the parameters the student sets, with at most linear interpolation between grid nodes, stated; a grid is never a fitter.

GRID: grid, nearest spectrum, closest spectrum, closest model, closest curve, looks closest, look closest, best-matching spectrum, best matching spectrum, best-matching model, rejilla, cuadricula, cuadrícula, espectro mas cercano, espectro más cercano, espectro mas parecido, espectro más parecido, se parece mas, se parece más. NEG: not, never, cannot, can't, does not, doesn't, no, nunca, jamas, jamás, sin, ni, no se.

peakFit.label: The bounded peak fit of the gate's prototype (a weighted quadratic by least squares, deliberately the simplest bounded method; the fitter authority of 154 and js/numeric/polyfit.js supply the least-squares step in the product kernel, and the oracle uses numpy lstsq).
peakFit.input: bins: centre ell_c (strictly increasing, finite), value D (finite) and sigma (finite, > 0), equal length >= 1; refusals: not-finite, bad-sigma, not-sorted, length-mismatch, empty.
peakFit.window: k = the index of the largest D; the window holds the bins with |ell_c - ell_c[k]| <= 75 multipoles (inclusive).
peakFit.model: t = (ell - ell_c[k]) / 75; D = a + b t + c t^2 by weighted least squares with weights 1/sigma^2; the apex is t* = -b / (2c), ell* = ell_c[k] + 75 t*.
peakFit.interval: sigma_ell = 75 sqrt(g^T V g) with g the gradient of t* with respect to (a, b, c) and V the coefficient covariance (A^T W A)^-1 (not rescaled by chi-square); the 68.27 percent interval is ell* +- sigma_ell and the 95.45 percent interval ell* +- 2 sigma_ell (the Gaussian delta-method intervals).
peakFit.notConstrained: In this order, the fit returns not-constrained with the first code that holds: too-few-bins (fewer than 5 bins in the window), no-curvature (c >= 0 or c / sigma_c > -5), apex-outside-window (|t*| > 1), interval-too-wide (2 sigma_ell > 150, the window's width). A not-constrained fit returns no apex and no interval number.
peakFit.whyFiveSigma: The window is centred on the largest bin, which is biased towards an upward fluctuation, so a flat noisy spectrum is concave more often than a coin; the 5 sigma curvature cut is the committed defence and leg E5 measures it.

syntheticPeak.label: DESIGN, not any measurement's, not the CMB's: a labelled synthetic binned spectrum with its truth manifest (7.5 rule 8). It has a skewed peak so that the quadratic fit is not exact; it says nothing about real spectra and recovery of it alone validates nothing for real data.

truth.form: D(ell) = base + amplitude exp(-(ell - ell0)^2 / (2 w^2)), w = widthBelow for ell < ell0, widthAbove otherwise; the maximum is at ell0 exactly.

syntheticPeak.binning: bin centres ell_c = u + width k for k = 0..N with u a uniform draw in [0, width) per draw ('grid phase') and the centres in [20, 700]; each bin's value is the truth at its centre (no averaging over the bin: a stated simplification), sigma = 0.015 D_true(ell_c) (relative), the data = D_true + sigma z, z standard normal.
syntheticPeak.noPeak: D = 3000 at every centre, sigma 0.015 D, the same binning; there is no peak.
syntheticPeak.coverageRule: a draw covers when ell0 lies in the interval of a fit that is not not-constrained; a not-constrained draw counts as NOT covering (so a fit that refuses often fails its leg); the rate is judged against the nominal 0.6827 (E1) and 0.9545 (E2) with a binomial three-sigma band sqrt(p (1 - p) / n) x 3, separately for the prototype and the oracle.

pinnedVectors.rule: three vectors without a random number: truth at width 30, grid phase u in {0, 10, 20}, with the deterministic perturbation e_i = 0.01 D_true(ell_c,i) sin(i (k + 1) + 0.3), k = 0, 1, 2 the vector's index, i the bin's index from 0, sigma = 0.015 D_true; the prototype and the oracle must agree on ell*, sigma_ell, c / sigma_c, the window's bin count and the code if not constrained.

verdict.rows: A leg with a group other than 'reported' and no 'expected: not-run' passes or fails by its bound; a leg with 'expected: not-run' is NOT RUN until its request is met; P1, P2 and P3 are NOT RUN if the extraction is ambiguous; a pass/fail leg that cannot be measured fails the gate on that threshold.
verdict.kernel: KERNEL PASS iff every leg of groups integrity, relation, oracle, ensemble, refusals, claim and grid-mechanics (G2, G3) passes, and P1, P2 and P3 each pass or are NOT RUN; otherwise KERNEL FAIL.
verdict.A: KERNEL PASS and S1 to S4, G1, C1, F1 and F2 all RUN and pass: the demonstration with the spectrum and the grid comparison.
verdict.B: KERNEL PASS and S1 to S4, F2 RUN and pass, while G1 is NOT RUN or fails: the demonstration with the spectrum alone.
verdict.C: KERNEL FAIL, or any S leg that ran fails, or any S leg NOT RUN: the relation alone as a reading step; 260's The pillars omits the CMB (Appendix C). A C reached because an S leg is NOT RUN is a C BY ABSENCE, not by failure, and is reported as NOT ESTABLISHED for A and B.
verdict.consumersClause: met iff the verdict is A or B. Whatever the verdict, no panel, lesson, guide, viewer, grid or spectrum file is built until Carl lifts the consumers rule.
verdict.partB: after A or B, and only after Carl goes ahead; not begun in this session; with C, there is no Part B (Appendix C: a reading step).

decisions.what: The conventions are committed as definitions and the data as requests: the binned spectrum, the Boltzmann-code outputs, the grid, the z_star and offset fitting formulas are published data or code outputs that this session neither fetches, runs nor types; they are requests S1, G1, F1, F2 and X1 with exact contents, and their legs are NOT RUN.
decisions.consequence: No A or B can be reached in this session; the verdict is at best C by absence.

decisions.what: z_star and the peak offset are INPUTS, not formulas: no fitting formula's coefficient is typed. r_s comes from the integral (the Eisenstein and Hu fit failed its legs in 257).
decisions.consequence: The geometry relation is validated end to end against an independent calculation and one published full calculation, without any cited formula.

decisions.what: The grid is a comparison drawn at the node nearest to the student's own parameters, with linear interpolation inside the grid and no extrapolation; the prototype has no function from a spectrum to a parameter through a grid (I2), and the claim rule is a test over strings (K1, K2).
decisions.consequence: No Hubble constant or composition is ever read from a grid label.

decisions.what: The peak fit is the simplest bounded method (a weighted quadratic in a window of +-75 multipoles about the largest bin) with a 5 sigma curvature cut; the synthetic ensemble is labelled DESIGN with a skewed peak, so coverage can fail by bias and a failure stays failing.
decisions.consequence: Coverage (E1, E2) and the false-positive rate (E5) are measured, not assumed.

decisions.what: P1 and P2 are NOT BLIND: the printed numbers were seen before this file was committed (seenBeforeCommitting); their bounds are stated by a rule written before any computation.
decisions.consequence: A pass says the integral reproduces a published full calculation at the stated precision; it does not say the model was tuned blind.
